query: How does resolution duration vary across incident category and priority?

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: Clean, well-separated categorical (database/email/vpn/network/etc.) directly named in the query; ideal grouping axis for comparing resolution duration.

per_column.name: affected_system
per_column.rationale: Interpretable system-level categories with reasonable cell counts; a finer but still meaningful segmentation to compare durations across.

per_column.name: incident_symptom_type
per_column.rationale: Symptom taxonomy (connectivity_failure, access_denied, outage, performance_degradation) is interpretable and plausibly associated with how long resolution takes; some NULLs but usable.

per_column.name: scope_indicator
per_column.rationale: Individual vs system_wide vs location_specific is a well-separated, intuitive scope axis strongly plausibly related to resolution effort/duration.

per_column.name: resolver_match
per_column.rationale: Boolean (assignee matched resolver) is interpretable and can be segmented on; plausible operational driver of duration, though somewhat imbalanced (403/97).

per_column.name: opened_hour_bucket
per_column.rationale: Business_hours/after_hours/overnight is a clean, interpretable temporal segmentation with balanced cells, a classic axis for exploring duration variation.

per_column.name: is_repeat_issue
per_column.rationale: Boolean repeat-issue flag is interpretable and groupable; recurrence plausibly relates to resolution duration.

per_column.name: caller_type
per_column.rationale: Named_employee vs itil_user is a clean binary segmentation that could reveal duration differences by caller class.

judge.rationale: All added columns are external, associational, and interpretable with well-separated, low-cardinality categories that can be grouped against resolution_duration. None merely restate the focus. incident_category directly echoes the existing 'category' field, and several flags are imbalanced (resolver_match, is_repeat_issue), slightly limiting comparative power, but as a set they open up multiple informative, human-readable segmentation axes (category, system, symptom, scope, timing, recurrence, caller type) well suited to exploratory analysis of duration.
